item.title: @fractal commented on "What interesting facts do you know about XOR?"
item.description: $$$a \oplus b < 2n \text{ for }a,b \le n$$$XOR can be represented using OR and AND$$$a \oplus b = (a \text{ OR } b) - (a \text{ AND } b)$$$XOR is self-inverse:$$$a \oplus b = c \Longleftrightarrow a=c \oplus b$$$Problems related to XOR often can be solved bitwise (for all of the bits independently)XOR is in fact addition in $$${Z}_{2}^{d}$$$ space, so many facts from linear algebra can be used in XOR related stuff (XOR basis is a good example)

item.title: @minuki646 commented on "2038L — Can anyone tell me why this greedy strategy works?"
item.description: I've solved this recently. Idk about editorials but I have my method of greedy.I greedily think the best way of optimize min planks = min waste woods.By looking at planks: - 60 = 21 + 21 + 18 (0 waste) — best choice - 60 ~ 25 + 25 (10 waste) — best choice for 25 type specifically - 60 ~ 18 + 18 + 18 (6 waste) — best choice for 18After greedily calculate the initial planks, carefully check the edge case when a 60 plank only used for 1 25 or 21, or 1-2 18.There you go, there's my code if you're interesting n = int(input()) n21 = n25 = n // 2 n18 = (n - n21) // 3 res = n18 + n21 + n25 b = c = n & 1 a = (n - n21) % 3 if a + b + c > 0: res += 1 if a + b + c > 2: res += 1 print(res)
